Plutarch, Moralia p. 293 a: τί τὸ φυξίμηλον; [What is the phyximēlon?] It is among the small and low-growing plants, whose shoots the grazing animals, coming upon them, cut short and injure and damage their growth. When, at any rate, they have shot up and attained size and escaped being harmed by those that come upon them, they are called phyximēla. The testimony of Aeschylus (fr. 377).
